title: Chicken Thighs With Butternut Squash and Gochujang
description:
By Yewande Komolafe: Gochujang, a Korean fermented chile paste, enlivens a straightforward dinner of roast
chicken and vegetables with a salty, spicy and umami-rich layer of flavor. Freshly grated ginger, sliced scallions
and quick-pickled radishes elevate the flavor even further. This recipe calls for a wintry mix of squash and
parsnips, but equal amounts of root vegetables like carrots, potatoes and beets, or lighter vegetables like
cauliflower, brussels sprouts or broccoli will work well too.
ingredients: 1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated (about 1 tablespoon)
4 tablespoons neutral oil, like grapeseed or canola, plus more for
1 pounds butternut squash, peeled, seeded and cut into 2-inch pieces
4-6 parsnips, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
4-6 scallions, ends trimmed, green and white parts separated, but not
6+ bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, drumsticks or breasts, patted dry
directions: Combine the gochujang, soy sauce, ginger and oil in a medium bowl or resealable bag. Season the chicken
with salt and toss to coat in the glaze in the bowl or bag.
Heat the oven to 425 degrees (see below for timing).
After 60 minutes (or less, if you’re in a hurry), add the squash, parsnips, and scallion whites, toss to coat
with glaze, or seal bag and shake to coat.
Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet. Arrange the chicken pieces skin-side up between the vegetables on the
Roast until vegetables are tender, chicken is cooked through and the skin crispy and browned in spots,
While the chicken cooks, thinly slice the scallion greens.
Using a sharp knife or a mandolin, cut the radishes into thin rounds. In a small bowl, toss the sliced
scallion greens and radishes with the rice vinegar and sesame oil, if using. Season to taste with salt and set
Top the roast chicken and vegetables with the quick-pickled scallion-radish mix and transfer to serving
Serve with steamed rice, if desired.
